concept: Foundation of the Indian National Congress
question: Who among the following had given the idea to mobilise all the leading Indian political leaders under a common platform called the Indian National Congress?
solution:
The correct answer is __**A O Hume**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A O Hume**, a retired British civil servant, was instrumental in the formation of the **Indian National Congress (INC)** in **1885**. He aimed to bring together prominent Indian leaders on a common platform to discuss and address issues of national importance.
 
• Hume's primary objective was to create a structured and peaceful platform for Indians to voice their grievances and demands to the British government, thus preventing any potential revolutionary uprisings.
 
• He played a vital role in uniting educated Indians and fostering a sense of national consciousness, paving the way for the future struggle for independence. Hence, A O Hume initiated the idea of the Indian National Congress.
 
• The first session of the Indian National Congress was held in **Bombay** in December 1885, under the presidency of **W C Bannerjee**, with the participation of seventy-two delegates from across India.
 
• Hume is often referred to as the **'Father of the Indian National Congress'** due to his pivotal role in its establishment. Hence, the correct answer is A O Hume.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About A O Hume:**

 
 
• **Allan Octavian Hume** (1829-1912) was a British civil servant and reformer who devoted himself to the cause of Indian political reform after his retirement.
 
• He believed in the need for a platform where Indians could present their demands in a constitutional manner to avoid violent uprisings.
 
• Hume played a unifying role in a politically diverse and fragmented society, laying the foundation for the Indian freedom movement.
 
 
 
• **Indian National Congress (INC):**
 
 
• The INC became the principal platform for Indian political aspirations, eventually evolving into the leading organization in the struggle for independence.
 
• Initially, the objectives of the INC included addressing administrative reforms, promoting unity, and ensuring increased participation of Indians in government.
 
• Over time, the INC became a mass movement, leading campaigns like the **Non-Cooperation Movement**, **Civil Disobedience Movement**, and the **Quit India Movement**.
 
 
 
• **Other notable figures:**
 
 
• **W C Bannerjee**: He was the first president of the INC and played a significant role in its early years.
 
• **Surendranath Bannerjee**: A prominent nationalist leader known for his efforts in promoting Indian self-rule and social reforms.
 
• **Ananda Mohan Bose**: A social reformer and nationalist who was also actively involved in Indian politics during the late 19th century.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of the INC Formation:**

 
 
• The INC provided a platform to unify Indians across regions, religions, and social backgrounds.
 
• Though initially a moderate organization, it laid the foundation for India's freedom movement, gradually adopting more radical approaches under leaders like **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**, **Mahatma Gandhi**, and others.
 
• The INC was instrumental in achieving India's independence in **1947**, marking the culmination of efforts initiated by A O Hume and other founding members.
